about: Elements and principles from the UC Berkeley design guide (guides.lib.berkeley.edu/design). Shared by the marks analysis call and the critique agent call. matrix[element][principle] lists the pairs a sketcher can work with through marks. A pair left out is skipped. Strong pairs get seed questions in question_bank.json. Weak pairs are used only when the AI sees them clearly.

line.definition: A straight or curved mark that connects two points or is the path of a moving point.

shape.definition: A two-dimensional enclosed area, geometric (hard edge) or organic (soft edge).

form.definition: A three-dimensional shape with height, width and depth.

space.definition: The distances and areas around, between and within components of a design.

value.definition: The degree of lightness or darkness in a color.

color.definition: The perception of light reflected from the surface of a shape or form.

texture.definition: The surface quality of an object that we can sense through touch.

balance.definition: The distribution of objects, colors, texture and space.

emphasis.definition: The part of the design that catches the viewer's attention.

movement.definition: The path the viewer's eye takes through the work.

pattern.label: Pattern & Repetition
pattern.definition: The repeating of an element all over the work.

rhythm.definition: One or more elements used repeatedly to create a feeling of organized movement.

proportion.definition: The relative size and scale of the various elements within a design.

variety.definition: The use of several elements of design to hold the viewer's attention.

unity.definition: The feeling of harmony between all parts of the design, which creates a sense of completeness.

balance.looks_for: Line weight spread across both sides.

movement.looks_for: Where the line takes the eye.

pattern.looks_for: Repeated lines, such as railings or mullions.

rhythm.looks_for: Repeated lines at a changing interval.

variety.looks_for: Straight and curved, thick and thin.

unity.looks_for: One line ties separate parts together.

balance.looks_for: A big shape against several small ones.

emphasis.looks_for: One shape differs in size or edge.

rhythm.looks_for: Repeated shapes at a changing size.

unity.looks_for: Shapes share an edge or form one silhouette.

balance.looks_for: A solid mass against an open area.

emphasis.looks_for: The form with the clearest depth.

pattern.looks_for: Repeated forms, such as columns or cars.

proportion.looks_for: The scale of near and far.

unity.looks_for: Overlapping forms read as one group.

balance.looks_for: An empty side against a busy side.

movement.looks_for: A gap or road the eye travels.

proportion.looks_for: Sky to ground, or subject to space.

unity.looks_for: Consistent layers from front to back.

emphasis.looks_for: The strongest light-dark at the focus.

movement.looks_for: A path of lights or darks.

proportion.looks_for: How much is dark against light.

variety.looks_for: A full range of values or only a few.

unity.looks_for: Three values hold the page together.
